sentences.text: Plourdosteus was a small, extinct arthrodire placoderm that lived in Euramerica during the Givetian and Frasnian stages of the Devonian.
A specimen of Plourdosteus canadensis measured 37.5 centimeters in length.
The genus Plourdosteus was described by Ørvig in 1951.
Four species have been assigned to the genus: P. canadensis, P. livonicus, P. mironovi, and P. trautscholdi.
The name Plourdosteus honors the Plourde family associated with Miguasha National Park.
There are 17 recorded fossil occurrences of Plourdosteus in the Paleobiology Database.
Plourdosteus was originally placed in the family Plourdosteidae, but this family was later deemed polyphyletic and discarded.
Plourdosteus is now classified as a member of the family Panxiosteidae.
A 2010 study identified Panxiosteidae as the sister group to Dunkleosteidae, forming the superfamily Dunkleosteoidea.
A 2016 study placed Panxiosteidae outside Dunkleosteoidea, instead as a sister group to Coccosteidae within the superfamily Coccosteoidea.
Plourdosteus lived between 387.95 and 372.15 million years ago during the Givetian to Frasnian periods.
